# FLUX 3 multi-reference

**Workflow:** [`flux3/flux3-multi-reference.json`](../flux3/flux3-multi-reference.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `flux3` |
| Nodes | 9 |
| Links | 7 |
| Paid API calls per run | **1** |

---

Several images into one FLUX 3 Image call, each named by its position: image 1 is the scene, the rest supply what goes into it.

**input_image** is *image 1*, **input_image_2** is *image 2*, and so on. Socket order is the meaning — swap two Load Image nodes and the prompt now describes a different request.

With `aspect_ratio` at **auto** the output takes image 1's frame. Put a different image first, or set the ratio, for another shape.

Up to **10** references in total. Connect one and the next socket appears. References can also be http(s) URLs in `image_urls`, one per line; they are numbered after the sockets.

Say how the images relate: *the person from image 1 wears the jacket from image 2 in the kitchen from image 3*.

`variation` is not sent to the API — flux-3-image has no seed. It is **fixed** here so a rerun with nothing changed costs nothing; bump it (or set it to *randomize*) for a fresh take. `expanded_prompt` is `result.prompt`, the prompt the model actually used after expanding yours.

## The prompt lives in one node

The **Shared Prompt** node feeds the prompt in this graph, so there is one
place to edit it. It emits a plain string, **not** a list. That is the difference between it and **Prompt
List**, which would make each node it feeds run once per line and multiply what the graph
costs.
